title: Welcome to {{assistantName}}
content:
# 👋 Hi, I'm {{assistantName}}

Think of me as the **strongest employee** on your team. I'm connected to 3,000+ of the tools you already work in, so hand me a job — including the long, multi-step ones nobody has time to sit through — and I go get the right data, run the whole workflow, and bring back **finished work**, using the context this team shares rather than just what is in this conversation.

And I do not live on your machine. Close the laptop, go to dinner, get on a plane: **the job keeps running in the cloud** and the finished work is here when you come back.

## 🎨 Making things is the easy end of my work

An image, a deck, a page: this is the simplest thing I do. It matters because everything else arrives the same way — as a **real artifact** you can open, send, and edit, not a description of one. And you never start from scratch: I keep **a library of templates you can reuse as they are**, and every example below came from one.

**Images** — campaign visuals, product illustrations, social graphics, ad creative. This one is the **Sunlit Gouache** illustration style.

```
Make a campaign visual for an independent bookshop in the Sunlit Gouache style: warm afternoon light through the window, wooden shelves, one person browsing.
```

![campaign-visual.jpg](<{{campaignVisualUrl}}>)

**Presentations** — a rough brief becomes a designed deck that is ready to present. This is the **Sunburst playroom** template: 15 slides, available in 19 themes.

```
Create a 15-slide launch deck for SproutPop, a playful habit-building app for remote teams introducing a shared 30-day wellness challenge. Present it to people and culture leaders with cover, agenda, launch story, audience pain points, product vision, feature tour, rollout timeline, activation moments, team, early metrics, testimonials, pricing, and next steps. Make it saturated, joyful, idea-led, and structured.
```

![sproutpop-launch-deck](<{{presentationArtifactUrl}}>)

**Websites** — a launch page, a portfolio, a menu, live on its own URL. This is the **Coastal Hotel** template: a crest-style hero, postcard cards, and travel editorial motion.

```
Build a one-page site for a small coastal hotel from the Coastal Hotel template: rooms, rates, the neighbourhood, and an enquiry form. Put it online when it looks right.
```

![coastal-hotel-example](<{{websiteArtifactUrl}}>)

## 🔍 Data most assistants cannot reach

I have **first-party integrations** with data sources you will not find behind a chat window. That is the difference between an answer and a report you can act on: the numbers, the sources that back them, and what I think you should do next. No API keys, no configuration. Send me one of these:

**[Social research]({{webServicesUrl}}/social-data)** — profiles, posts, comments, and video transcripts across six platforms

```
Find the creators talking about small-business bookkeeping on TikTok and YouTube this month. Give me audience size, what they cover, and links.
```

**[Find people and creators]({{webServicesUrl}}/people-search)** — people by role, employer, skill, or location, with sources

```
Find 20 heads of customer support at Series A to C SaaS companies in Europe, with a link to each profile.
```

**[News and web search]({{webServicesUrl}}/web-search)** — ranked public-web results, filtered by recency and domain

```
What was announced about AI agents in the last 7 days? Group it by company and keep the sources.
```

**[SEO and keywords]({{webServicesUrl}}/seo-data)** — live search results, ranking keywords, backlink totals

```
Which keywords does our top competitor rank for that we do not, and which ones are worth writing about?
```

**[Market data]({{webServicesUrl}}/market-data)** — company profiles, latest quotes, price history

```
Compare the last 12 months of NVDA and AMD and tell me what moved each one.
```

**[Read any page]({{webServicesUrl}}/web-scraping)** — a public page turned into clean text or a list of links

```
Read this pricing page and turn it into a table I can compare with ours: [paste the URL]
```

## ⚙️ Workflows other teams have already built here

These are real workflows built on {{assistantName}}, each one with **the finished output attached**. Take a look for ideas:

- [Weekly growth report]({{workflowExamplesUrl}}/website-analytics-to-weekly-growth-report) — traffic and product behavior reconciled into one weekly read
- [Inbox morning brief]({{workflowExamplesUrl}}/daily-inbox-triage) — a day of email sorted into answer, waiting, and noise
- [Sales meeting follow-up]({{workflowExamplesUrl}}/sales-call-to-follow-up-draft) — a deal brief, CRM notes, and the follow-up email as a draft
- [Weekly paid ads review]({{workflowExamplesUrl}}/weekly-paid-ads-optimization) — where the budget went and what to change next week
- [Brief to landing page]({{workflowExamplesUrl}}/brand-brief-to-landing-page) — a brief becomes a live page, deployed and shareable
- [Recording to explainer video]({{workflowExamplesUrl}}/screen-recording-to-explainer-video) — a screen recording becomes a narrated explainer

Or describe yours and I will set it up here:

```
Every weekday morning, turn my last 24 hours of email into a brief: what needs an answer, what is waiting on someone else, and what is noise.
```

## 🛠️ Make it yours

**Start from a template, not a blank page.** Open **Template** in the chat composer, choose **Workflow**, and filter by the work you do.

![The workflow template picker, filtered by role]({{workflowTemplatePickerUrl}})

Run it once, **save what worked as your own workflow**, then give it a schedule so it runs without anyone asking. [Browse the templates]({{origin}}/)

**Or just talk it out with me.** Work the task through in conversation, correct me until the result is right, then save that as your own workflow. Other products call this a skill; here it also carries the automation with it — the connectors it needs, a schedule, and permissions — so next time it runs without anyone asking. [The docs]({{wwwUrl}}/docs) go through the advanced patterns.

**Give a job its own agent.** You start with me. When a job has its own rules, give it an agent of its own: its own instructions, its own access, its own workflows. Set **Visibility** to **Public** and the whole workspace can work with it, each person connecting their own accounts.

![Creating a new agent, with visibility set to private]({{newAgentDialogUrl}})

```
Create an agent for customer support and keep it private for now.
```

## 💬 I can work where your team already talks

This chat is one interface, not the only one. Mention me in a Slack channel and **the answer lands in the thread** on your message, so the channel is not flooded and the team can still follow it.

![{{assistantName}} in Slack: a channel mention answered in the thread](<{{slackSceneUrl}}>)

In a direct message, on Slack or Telegram, we keep one private conversation that holds its context between tasks. Briefs arrive on schedule; anything I draft waits for you to send it.

![{{assistantName}} in Telegram: a scheduled morning brief and a drafted reply](<{{telegramSceneUrl}}>)

[Set up Slack and Telegram]({{worksUrl}}) — and if the channel your team lives in is not there yet, [tell our team]({{wwwUrl}}/en/support) and we will take care of it for you.

## 💸 Mind which model I run on

Most of the work does not need the most advanced model. **Start cheap**, move up only when the result falls short — and keep **one thread to one job**, because every reply carries the whole conversation with it.

![Model tiers and thread hygiene: start cheap, move up only when the work is hard, and keep one thread to one job](<{{modelTiersUrl}}>)

👉 [How to reduce AI agent costs without using it less]({{wwwUrl}}/en/blog/posts/reduce-ai-agent-costs)

## 📸 A walkthrough in real screenshots

Six steps captured from the real product, for your reference: first prompts, a workflow template, connectors, saving your own workflow, a schedule, your own agent, and inviting the team.

![{{assistantName}} quick start](<{{quickStartUrl}}>)

Then: [invite your teammates]({{inviteUrl}}) so what you build is reusable on day one, and [read the docs]({{wwwUrl}}/docs) for how shared agents and workflows work.
